column1: # The build tools this lane pins: hashed, licensed, and recorded here rather
# than resolved by a build file.
# **Nothing here ships.** OkHttp, Okio and `kotlin-stdlib` were removed when the
# floor moved to API 29: their only unique value was ALPN below 29, and at 29
# `SSLParameters.setApplicationProtocols` is public. What is left is R8, which
# rewrites the artifact and is not in it.
# A version range or a `+` would make the artifact that ships differ from the
# artifact that was reviewed, which is the whole of a supply-chain problem in
# one line. These are exact versions and exact SHA-256 digests of the exact
# jars, and the test that uses them verifies the digest before putting a jar on
# a classpath -- so a substituted artifact fails the build rather than shipping.
# The digests were taken from the jars fetched from Maven Central, each of
# which also matched the SHA-1 published alongside it. Two independent digests
# of the same bytes, which is the most the registry offers.
# The zero-invokedynamic rule is NOT applied to these. It is a rule about
# NTS-authored Java, kept so the artifacts this repository builds stay legible
# and desugar predictably; a third-party jar is reviewed on its own terms and
# passes through D8 like any other dependency.
# `scope` is `runtime` for anything that ships inside the APK and `tool` for
# anything that only builds it. R8 is a tool: it rewrites the artifact and is
# not in it, so it is pinned for reproducibility rather than reviewed as a
# dependency -- but a build tool that can be swapped silently is a supply-chain
# problem of exactly the same shape, which is why it is in the same file.
# `license` is an SPDX identifier and not the whole of the obligation -- but the
# rest of that obligation is currently empty, because **nothing here ships**.
# R8 rewrites the artifact and is not in it, so no recipient of the APK receives
# it and none of the redistribution duties attach.
# Kept, because this was measured and OkHttp may return for devices below 29:
# none of `okhttp`, `okio-jvm` or `kotlin-stdlib` carries a `META-INF/NOTICE` or
# `META-INF/LICENSE`, checked by listing the jars rather than inferred from the
# license field, so Apache-2.0 section 4(d) had nothing to propagate and the
# remaining duty was 4(a), a packaging step in the consuming app. And OkHttp
# ships its own R8 rules at `META-INF/proguard/okhttp3.pro`, applied
# automatically to an app that bundles it and not by anything here.
# `repository` because they are not all in one place. R8 is published to
# Google's Maven and not to Central, and a fetcher that assumed one host would
# quietly fail over to "cannot reach the network" for an artifact that is
# simply somewhere else.
# group
com.android.tools
